description: Build the state layer and layout compute that live OUTSIDE React's render tree: (a) a vanilla Zustand store owning scene data in pre-allocated plain typed arrays with a free-list for node-slot recycling and dirty-range tracking; (b) a pure diff-apply function that mutates those arrays in place from graph diffs {addedNodes, removedNodes, updatedEdges}; (c) a Web Worker running the d3-force-3d simulation that reads/writes the shared buffers off the main thread; (d) the scoring->visual mapping (impact->size, freshness->emissive/color, category/sentiment->color). This feature is pure logic + worker plumbing with NO R3F/Canvas code, so it is fully unit-testable in-sandbox. It is the foundation the FEAT-003 engine consumes.
steps: Create lib/graph3d/types.ts defining the internal scene-buffer contract: a GraphDiff type {addedNodes: EconomicNode[], removedNodes: string[], updatedEdges: EconomicEdge[]} (align field names with lib/types.ts) plus buffer-layout constants (CAPACITY ceiling for nodes/edges, floats-per-node for the instance matrix/color/impact/freshness/selected attributes).

Create lib/graph3d/store.ts: a VANILLA Zustand store (import { createStore } from 'zustand/vanilla' - NOT the React hook) created OUTSIDE React. It owns pre-allocated Float32Array/Uint32Array typed arrays sized to the capacity ceiling for: instance matrices (or position+scale), per-instance color, impact, freshness, selected; plus edge index/endpoint arrays. It maintains: a Map from node id -> slot index, a free-list (stack of recycled slot indices) so removed nodes free their slot for reuse, a count of live nodes, and dirty-range bookkeeping (min/max touched instance index, or a dirty set) that the render loop will consume and clear. Expose imperative methods: initFromGraph(GraphData), applyDiff(GraphDiff), setSelected(id|null), setFilters(...), consumeDirtyRange()->{start,count} then clear, and selector-friendly slices for the HUD (counts, selected node metadata, active filters). ZERO per-call heap allocation in applyDiff's hot path where feasible (reuse scratch objects; document any unavoidable allocation).

Create lib/graph3d/applyDiff.ts (or fold into store.ts) implementing the pure diff-apply: added nodes take a slot from the free-list (or the next free index up to CAPACITY; if at capacity, drop-with-warning rather than throw), write their visual attributes, and register id->slot; removed nodes clear their attributes, return their slot to the free-list, and delete the id mapping; updated edges rewrite edge endpoint/strength arrays. Mark dirty ranges for every touched slot. Guarantee slot recycling: a node removed then a new node added reuses the freed slot (this is the fix for the prototype's filter-toggle leak).

Create lib/graph3d/visualMapping.ts: pure functions mapping domain fields to GPU attributes - impact (economicImpactScore/val) -> instance scale; freshnessScore -> emissive intensity and fresh/recent/older tint; category -> base color (domestic #22c55e, international #3b82f6, economic #f59e0b, political #ef4444); a sentiment derivation identical to the backend/REST rule (score>=7 positive, <=3 negative, else neutral) -> optional sentiment tint for the heatmap overlay; and article-age -> Z depth for the time-axis projection. Keep these allocation-free (write into passed-in typed-array offsets or return primitives).

Create lib/graph3d/forceWorker.worker.ts: a Web Worker that runs d3-force-3d (forceSimulation with forceManyBody/forceLink/forceCenter plus per-category attractor forces for clustering; edge strength sets the link spring constant). It receives node/edge topology + filter visibility via postMessage (or a SharedArrayBuffer if the build supports it; otherwise transfer typed arrays), ticks the simulation off the main thread, and posts back updated positions. Document in a header comment WHY a worker sim (not GPGPU) was chosen for Step 2 (keeps main thread free; GPGPU is a later optimization). Provide a thin main-thread wrapper lib/graph3d/forceSimClient.ts that starts/stops the worker, feeds topology/visibility, and writes returned positions into the store's typed arrays + marks dirty ranges. Guard worker creation so it no-ops in a non-browser/SSR/test context.

Add unit tests under test/ (or co-located *.test.ts) run by `bun test`, covering: (1) applyDiff adds nodes into free slots and writes correct attributes; (2) removing a node frees its slot and a subsequent add REUSES that exact slot index (free-list recycling / leak fix); (3) capacity ceiling: adding beyond CAPACITY drops-with-warning and does not corrupt existing slots or throw; (4) dirty-range bookkeeping reports the touched range and clears on consume; (5) visualMapping: impact->scale monotonic, freshness->emissive mapping, category->color exact hex, sentiment derivation matches the >=7/<=3 rule, age->Z ordering (older = further). Keep worker code out of these tests (test the pure functions and store directly); if the worker wrapper is tested, stub the Worker global.
Do NOT touch app/network/page.tsx or delete NetworkGraph.tsx in this feature (that happens in FEAT-003). This feature only adds the lib/graph3d/* modules and their tests.
acceptance_criteria: lib/graph3d/store.ts exports a vanilla Zustand store (created via zustand/vanilla, not a React hook) that owns pre-allocated typed arrays and is usable outside React.
applyDiff mutates the typed arrays in place; a remove-then-add sequence provably reuses the freed slot index (verified by a passing test).
Adding nodes beyond the CAPACITY ceiling is handled gracefully (drop-with-warning, no throw, existing data intact) and is covered by a test.
visualMapping functions produce the exact category hex colors and a sentiment derivation matching the backend/REST >=7 positive / <=3 negative / else neutral rule, covered by tests.
A d3-force-3d Web Worker (lib/graph3d/forceWorker.worker.ts) plus a main-thread client wrapper exist; the wrapper no-ops safely when Worker is unavailable (SSR/test).
`bun test` passes all new store/diff/free-list/visual-mapping unit tests.
`bun run build` and `bun run lint` remain green (no new warnings beyond the pre-existing NetworkGraph ones).
verification: Run `bun test` and confirm all FEAT-002 unit tests pass (diff-apply, free-list recycling, capacity ceiling, dirty-range, visual mapping).
Run `bun run build` and confirm exit 0.
Run `bun run lint` and confirm no new warnings beyond the two pre-existing NetworkGraph warnings.
